checklist.notes: The model and production task target narrative order, make a decision, and contrastive information focus as required.
The overall model-notice-focus-transform sequence is sound, but the event-numbering task has no determinable answer from the supplied text.
The lesson uses previously introduced past forms and word stress before introducing narrative sequence, the collocation, and sentence stress.
The sequencing markers and prominence examples are clear, but “number the events 1–4” conflicts with the number and grouping of events in the model.
Three coordinated targets are adequately bounded by one short account and a four-event final production.
The class, rain, umbrella, and library context is accessible, and no unsupported population-wide learning claim is made.
Apart from the ambiguous event count, the noticing and transformation stages lead consistently to the stated sequencing, collocation, and focus outcome.

findings.description: The model contains more than four candidate events or states—walking, rain starting, opening the umbrella, wind breaking it, deciding/waiting, rain stopping, and leaving—yet the learner is told to “number the events 1–4.” No rule identifies which four or how to group them, so a solo learner cannot complete or check this central sequencing task reliably.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the model to contain exactly four explicitly bounded events plus a separately labeled background, or instruct the learner to label the background and number every completed event with a supplied model answer.

methods: Inspected the lesson against its reconstructed, hash-matched M5 teaching payload and confirmed that no external source payload was supplied.
Compared wording and examples across the closed set of all ten revised lessons for suspicious verbatim duplication beyond shared instructional scaffolding.
Reviewed the audit provenance/copyright result and source-scope constraints as machine evidence without treating them as a web-wide originality check.
copyright_originality_check.scope_limitations: Closed-corpus review of the ten supplied lessons plus their exact M5/request/audit context only; no Internet-wide search, external proprietary corpus, legal opinion, or provider receipt was available.

limitations: This is an independent AI pedagogical review for development evidence only; it is not human review, release approval, certification, or publication authorization.
The governing M5 snapshot retains DRAFT taxonomy and OUTLINE_ONLY curriculum records and is limited to the development lane.
No learner trial, classroom observation, or outcome study was performed.
No audio was supplied, so no acoustic, listening-performance, or pronunciation-performance review was performed.
Originality checking was closed-corpus and artifact-bound; no web-wide plagiarism search, external corpus comparison, or legal determination was performed.
Generation provider provenance was not independently established; UNKNOWN is retained rather than inferred.
Generator reasoning, self-assessment, and prior review records were not inspected.
